title: Epistolae
author: Constantinus Imperator
source: Translated by Claude from tmp79.tmp79.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

passages.original: Jubet imperator ut Jihrl Arii igni tradantur.
passages.english: The emperor orders that the books of Arius be committed to the fire.
passages.notes: "Jihrl" is a scanning error, evidently for "libri" (books).

passages.original: Illud vero valde in eo urbanum est, quod sub persona pudoris tanto studio silentium simulet. Mitem et mansuetum te palam exhi- bes, cum malarum artium et insidiarum plenus multos fallas. Sed, o miseriam! diabolus ut voluit, Arium nobis iniquitatis officinam fecit. Accede ac dic mihi fidei tuae documentum, et nequaquam ta- ceas. Heus! tu qui os obtortum et ingenium ab om- nem improbitatem possides : unum dicis Deum? me suffragatorem habes : sic igitur sentias.
passages.english: But this is very witty in him, that under the guise of modesty he feigns silence with such great zeal. You show yourself openly gentle and mild, while, full of evil arts and snares, you deceive many. But, oh misery! The devil, as he wished, has made Arius a workshop of iniquity for us. Come forward and tell me the proof of your faith, and by no means keep silent. Hey! You who possess a twisted mouth and a mind [inclined] to every wickedness: do you say [there is] one God? You have me as a supporter: so, then, hold that view.
passages.notes: "ab omnem" is read as "ad omnem" (toward every). The passage shifts between the third and second person, addressing Arius directly.

passages.original: Illud modo favere aliquatenus potest, quod Hele- nam matrem suam, cum antea pietatem minime esset imbuta, Constantinum piam admodum reddidisse scripserit Eusebius : ex quo potuisse aliquando eam a calumniis Judaeorum in fraudem induci, minime abhorret. Adde revera in suis pandectis veternosos illos homines passim blasphemare, Christum nos- trum propter maleficia fuisse cruce multatum.
passages.english: Only this can lend it some support: that Eusebius wrote that Constantine made his mother Helena very pious, although before she had been little imbued with piety. From this it is not at all implausible that she could at some time have been led into deception by the calumnies of the Jews. Add that in fact in their pandects those antiquated men everywhere blaspheme [by saying] that our Christ was punished with the cross for evil deeds.
passages.notes: "Pandectis" (pandects) presumably refers to the Jewish compilations, i.e. the Talmud. Scanning hyphenations ("Hele- nam", "nos- trum") have been joined.

passages.original: Hortatur imperator populum Antiochiae ne Eusebium de sede episcopali Caesareae dimoveat.
passages.english: The emperor urges the people of Antioch not to remove Eusebius from the episcopal see of Caesarea.

passages.original: Imperator Eusebii orationem de Pascha laudat.
passages.english: The emperor praises Eusebius' oration on Easter.
